newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Germany critical of Israel in Mideast talks -paper.
newsitem.headline: Germany critical of Israel in Mideast talks -paper.

text.p: Israel's ambassador to Germany reported that Bonn was deeply critical of Israel's stance in peace talks, the Yedioth Ahronoth newspaper said on Friday.

Ambassador Avi Primor in a recent report also wrote that German officials told him leaders in the Netherlands and U.S. peace envoy Dennis Ross expressed disappointment after recent meetings with Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu, the Israeli daily said.
Primor also wrote that he had been told Ross had informed the Germans that Israel was mainly to blame for the crisis in Middle East peace moves.
A foreign ministry official said Israel did not usually comment on such reports.

"The Germans believe the claims that they are hearing from the Arab side saying we behave arrogantly in negotiations with our neighbours, humiliate them and create a destructive atmosphere," the paper quoted Primor as saying.
Primor said he based his comments on discussions with "the most senior officials" in Chancellor Helmut Kohl's office and the German foreign ministry.

"From Dennis Ross they heard that after his last visit to the Middle East and the prime minister's visit to the United States he was also very disappointed and placed blame for the present crisis principally on us," the newspaper quoted him saying.

Peace talks between Israel and the Palestinians ground to a halt after Israel began a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem on March 18. The move sparked almost daily clashes between Palestinians and Israeli troops.
The United States, sponsor of the Middle East peace process launched in 1991, has tried to revive talks. The EU is also trying to find a way to bring the sides together.
